text:
Situation: Carboplatin has been on the FDA drug shortage list since 2023-04-28 and remains listed as of 2026-10-21, a duration of 42 months. Corvale East holds 54 units of the Teva product (NDC 00703423901) and 77 units of the Apotex product (NDC 60505628201), providing 18 days of supply at current use. Corvale Lakeside has only 4 units total, equating to 1.9 days of supply. Corvale General holds approximately 76 units across three listings, providing 9 days of supply.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the carboplatin shortage on 2023-04-28. An inspection of Intas Pharmaceuticals Limited (FEI 3004011473) ended 2022-12-02 and was classified OAI, with the classification letter dated 2023-04-05. Import alert 66-40 for Intas was published 2023-06-01 and again 2023-11-14, and a Warning Letter was issued 2023-07-28. Multiple manufacturers remain in current shortage status per FDA, including Accord Healthcare (supplied by Intas), Teva, Fresenius Kabi, Hospira/Pfizer, Eugia, Gland Pharma, Avyxa, and Teyro Labs.

Our position: Corvale East has sufficient inventory to support internal transfers while maintaining a two-week buffer. P&T has previously approved interchange between the Teva and Apotex products (same product, alternate manufacturer) and between Accord and Teva (same molecule, alternate concentration or vial size).

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 26 vials from Corvale East to Corvale Lakeside — needs pharmacy director approval of transfer request.
2. Transfer 2 vials from Corvale East to Corvale General — needs pharmacy director approval of transfer request.
3. Dispense Apotex carboplatin 10 mg/mL as same product, alternate manufacturer per existing P&T approval — needs pharmacist verification at dispensing.
4. Dispense Teva carboplatin 10 mg/mL as same molecule, alternate concentration or vial size per existing P&T approval — needs pharmacist verification at dispensing.

Not recommended: No new clinical protocol changes or alternative agent substitutions at this time.
